subjects.subject: quality-gates

subjects.subject: prompt-assembly

subjects.subject: voice-io
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/provider.ts:94 A grep search across the LLM provider files for voice, speech, audio, and synthesis found no speech I/O capabilities, as the abstraction defines static repository assessment methods (`assess`) evaluating git metadata and code files to produce maturity scores.

subjects.subject: test-harness
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/bedrock.test.ts:19 The suite stubs external cloud LLM providers with hand-written in-memory mocks without recorded network interaction fixtures or scheduled live certification lanes.

subjects.subject: agent-cli-transport
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/transport/claude.ts:109 The authorization probe inherits credentials that real runs strip, so it can report authorization for a different billing environment.

subjects.subject: codebase-scanning
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/json.ts:15-23,74-150 parseJsonLoose never silently drops a malformed model reply: fast parse -> fenced-block recovery -> jsonc cleanup -> balanced-brace scan, and total failure throws a typed ProviderParseError with a truncated snippet rather than degrading silently. Realizes llm-assisted-scanning's 'model as unreliable sensor, malformed output counted not dropped' discipline. Contrast: the sibling 'Scan Pipeline & Ingestion' context is recorded deviation for governance/posture/exposure fetches still doing .catch(()=>null) with score-bearing folds — this parsing layer is markedly more careful than that sibling ingestion layer, i.e. the discipline is uneven across the same pipeline's own stages.

subjects.subject: settings
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/config.ts:43 Malformed numeric LLM configuration silently becomes the default without the corruption diagnostic required by typed accessors.

subjects.subject: multi-provider-gateway-plane
subjects.evidence: src/lib/scan-assess.ts:353 The multi-provider attempt loop continues after any non-client exception without router-versus-candidate attribution, allowing an application-side defect to consume subsequent candidates.

subjects.subject: browser-credential-boundary

Separately noted (not scored as a technique deviation): leaderboard/page.tsx:98-101 renders getDbMode()/dbModeLabel() ('Served live from Aurora DSQL') to every anonymous visitor of this crawlable public page — the SAME value api/health/route.ts:29-38 explicitly reasons 'describes deployment TOPOLOGY... shouldn't be handed to an anonymous caller' and gates behind CRON_SECRET. I did not mark this a deviation because it discloses only a coarse backend-family label (no hostname/credential/error-body), and the codebase treats it as a deliberate trust-building UI element (also on the landing page, IndexGallery.tsx) rather than an oversight — but it is a real inconsistency in how the project applies its own stated topology-disclosure rule, worth registry attention.
